title: Java Fundamentals
description: Core Java: types, classes, collections, exceptions and the JVM. 20 questions across all question types.

questions.prompt: Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed?
questions.explanation: A final class cannot be extended (String is a well-known example).

questions.prompt: What is the default value of an int field that is never assigned?
questions.explanation: Numeric fields default to 0; only local variables must be assigned before use.

questions.prompt: Which collection does NOT allow duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: A Set (such as HashSet) stores each element at most once.

questions.prompt: What does JVM stand for?
questions.explanation: The Java Virtual Machine runs compiled Java bytecode on any platform.

questions.prompt: Which method signature is the entry point of a standalone Java program?
questions.explanation: The JVM looks for public static void main(String[] args) to start a program.

questions.prompt: Which exceptions must be either caught or declared with throws?
questions.explanation: The compiler enforces handling of checked exceptions like IOException.

questions.prompt: String objects in Java are...
questions.explanation: A String can't change after creation; operations like concat return a new String.

questions.prompt: Which keyword makes a class inherit from another class?
questions.explanation: extends is for class inheritance; implements is for interfaces.

questions.prompt: Which of these are primitive types?
questions.explanation: int, boolean and double are primitives; String and Integer are classes.

questions.prompt: Which are access modifiers in Java?
questions.explanation: Java has public, protected, private and package-private (no keyword); internal is Kotlin/C#.

questions.prompt: Which interfaces belong to the Java Collections Framework?
questions.explanation: List, Set and Map are collection interfaces; Runnable is for threads.

questions.prompt: A Java class can extend more than one class.
questions.explanation: Java has single class inheritance; a class can implement many interfaces instead.

questions.prompt: The fields of a record class are final.
questions.explanation: Record components become private final fields, which makes records shallowly immutable.

questions.prompt: The == operator compares the contents of two String objects.
questions.explanation: == compares references; use equals() to compare contents.

questions.prompt: The ___ keyword creates a new object instance.
questions.explanation: new allocates an object and calls its constructor.

questions.prompt: A method with the same name as its class and no return type is called a ___.
questions.explanation: Constructors initialise new objects.

questions.prompt: How many bits does a Java int use?
questions.explanation: int is a 32-bit signed integer; long is 64-bit.

questions.prompt: Put the steps from source code to a running program in order.
items: Compile it with javac into bytecode (.class)
The class loader loads the classes into the JVM
questions.explanation: Source is compiled to bytecode, which the JVM loads and runs (interpreted and JIT-compiled).

questions.prompt: Order these integer types from smallest to largest.
questions.explanation: byte is 8 bits, short 16, int 32 and long 64.

questions.prompt: Match each keyword with what it means.

pairs.right: Belongs to the class, not an instance
Can't be reassigned, overridden or extended
Must be implemented by a subclass
Only one thread runs it at a time per lock

questions.explanation: These modifiers control ownership, mutability, inheritance and thread safety.
